newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania sees low interest in '97 selloff list.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania sees low interest in '97 selloff list.

text.p: Lithuania's privatisation agency said on Thursday that the vast majority of the 835 companies in which the state intends to sell its stakes in 1997 are of little interest to foreign investors.
"Out of the 835 companies, only 32 are attractive to foreign investors," the head of the country's privatisation agency, Vytis Atkochiunas, told a news conference.
"Foreign investors are interested only in the companies in which they can acquire at least 51 percent of the shares in and which have no less than 100 employees," he said.
Atkochiunas said the top companies included a Vilnius manufacturer of household cleaning products, a drill factory, a machine-tool factory and several textile factories.
A separate list with 14 key firms in the transport, energy and communications sectors was unveiled earlier this month.
"The privatisation programmes for these 14 companies will be prepared by financial consultants which will be chosen by bids," Eduardas Vilkas, the head of the privatisation commission, said.
"The process should be carried out by open bids, to avoid the mistakes made by our neighbours," he added.
